ai_show_review.summary: Scorching early‑Dead set with Rider, Mindbender & Cream Puff War
ai_show_review.blurb: The May 19 1966 Avalon show crackles with high‑energy blues and the band’s first taste of psychedelia. Standout moments include a blistering "I Know You Rider," a rare "Mindbender" and a ferocious "Cream Puff War." The vintage soundboard capture preserves Pigpen’s organ punch and Bill Kreutzmann’s booming bass drum.
ai_show_review.review: On May 19, 1966 the Grateful Dead took the Avalon Ballroom into overdrive. From the opening “Beat It On Down The Line” through a relentless second set the band blended gritty blues covers with fledgling originals, never missing a beat. Jerry Garcia’s guitar was on fire – his solos on "I Know You Rider" and especially the rare "Mindbender" are nothing short of scorching, even if some listeners note his tone was still developing. Phil Lesh laid down an “on‑fire” bass foundation that kept the groove tight, while Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming—particularly the thunderous bass drum on "Viola Lee Blues" and "Cream Puff War"—adds a front‑of‑stage punch that shines through the vintage two‑channel mix. Pigpen’s organ solo on “Good Lovin’” and his gritty vocals throughout give the show its early‑Dead character. The soundboard source (gd66-05-19.sbd.lestatkat.6516.sbeok.shnf) captures this energy with crisp, balanced clarity, making it the definitive listening experience for anyone wanting to hear the band at a pivotal moment of blues‑rock intensity and nascent psychedelia.

best_recording.reason: Excellent vintage clarity, balanced mix with prominent drums and Pigpen, captures the scorching Rider, Mindbender and Cream Puff War performances.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers blistering solos on "Rider" and a fiery, vibrato‑laden lead on the rare "Mindbender," though some note his tone is still maturing.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides an energetic, sweet‑toned bass that locks in tightly with the drums; praised especially for his work on "Mindbender."
band_performance.Bob: Bob Weir receives little specific mention; one reviewer found his take on "New Minglewood Blues" lackluster.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann’s drumming is highlighted as fantastic, with a powerful bass drum that propels "Viola Lee Blues" and "Cream Puff War."

must_listen_sequences: Beat It On Down The Line
